Metal Gear Solid and Metal Gear Solid 3 would probably be your best starting point since their stories are relatively independent of other games in the series.

I started from the MGS I: Twin Snakes (a less clunky version of MGS I) and went to II and III and so forth eventually. I recommend going through the main games first (I, II, III, IIII) and then going back into the side games (The games released on PSP like Portable Ops are really just padding onto the story, but still fun) If you want to start out without being confused you could read up on the story from the original Metal Gear games that were released on PSX.
If I did that I might have to go buy a nes. I want to know what the most recent game to catch up I can play is

You can probably just wait for 5 and play that. If you want to play release order you can just start with MGS on PS1.

Chronological is also an option.
They both come with MGS3:Subsistence, HD Collection and the Legacy Collection. Also extremely easy to emulate. You can skip straight to MGS, if you want.
metal gear solid 4, metal gear rising: revengeance. revengeance is about raiden but its an epic play

The NES games aren't needed to get the full story of the modern games. This collection includes MGS 1-4, plus the MSX versions of Metal Gear and Metal Gear 2, which are the canon versions. Get this and play them in numbered order. Peace walker isn't needed for the overall story here, but probably ties into 5. Likewise, the MSX games aren't really needed either, so they can be played whenever.

At some point, I also would play Metal Gear Rising. While not necessary for the overall story, it is insanely fun. It doesn't really spoil much of anything for the main series, so play it whenever.

Start with Metal Gear Solid 1. Take your time and go through the dialogue. I'd suggest playing through it more than once even. The games can be somewhat hard to grasp if you don't take the time to listen to what's going on. There are also loads of easter eggs.
I'd recommend MGS1 (Twin Snakes if you have a Gamecube, PSN if not), MGS2, MGS3, Peace Walker, then MGS4.

As a huge Metal Gear fan I am going to say not to worry about the story to much right now.

The Phantom pain is going to be great based on game play mechanics alone. If you want to be up to date for The Phantom Pain (1984) then all you need to play is MGS3 and Peace Walker. You will have everything you need to understand the story.

Anything g beyond that is just gravy that takes place after 1985.
If you have a 360 you can buy 2 of the Metal Gear games digitally that were for PS2 previously.

Start with 3, its recent enough that it shouldn't be too hard to get into and on top of that it's a prequel to the rest of the main series. The order of the main games is 3-peace walker-ground zeroes-5-1-2-4. I think portable ops falls in before peace walker, and revengeance takes place after 4.

Metal Gear Solid is a good start to be fair. The story and characters in it are great and it never felt like I had to play the NES ones to be up to date with the story. I think it's a good baseline in the way if you didn't happen to like that one I definitely wouldn't recommend the others.
